transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, Diego and Karen from security/solutions will jump in. Could folks from Crestview introduce?
[00:08] Lena Martin: Hi, Lena Martin, CISO at Crestview Health. We run compliance and security for the platform.
[00:11] Arjun Patel: Arjun, IT Security Manager.
[00:13] Samantha Lee: Sam, Compliance.
[00:15] Noah Kim: Noah, Cloud Architect.
[00:17] Maya Patel: Awesome, thank you. The purpose today is a posture review — SOC 2 and ISO 27001 — go through reports, Trust Center access, controls mapping, and surface any gaps. We'll try to keep to about 45-60 minutes.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: Quick note, transcription might have a few mis-hearings, apologies for any names. I'll start with an overview of what Redwood can share as part of our trust materials.
[00:37] Diego Ramos: We have a SOC 2 Type II report covering common criteria, we can share through a gated Trust Center link, we also have ISO 27001 certificate and mappings. For customers with enterprise contracts we provide reviewer access to the Trust Center.
[00:52] Samantha Lee: When you say reviewer access, what level of docs are available? Full report or redacted?
[00:58] Karen Zhou: Usually full SOC 2 Type II report under NDA, plus a controls matrix that maps our controls to SOC criteria and ISO clauses. There may be some redactions around vendor specifics, but the control testing narratives are intact.
[01:12] Lena Martin: Great. Crestview needs the full report for our internal audit and also a controls mapping into our ISMS. We also need to know about any subprocessor list and change history.
[01:22] Diego Ramos: Subprocessors list is in the Trust Center; we also include a history of material changes. For high-risk customers we can export a CSV of subprocessors.
[01:33] Noah Kim: On technical side, can you walk us through RBAC and SSO options? We use Okta with SCIM provisioning.
[01:40] Diego Ramos: Sure — we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync, RBAC is role-based with least-privilege roles. You can map Okta groups to Redwood roles and we also have an audit trail for admin activity. Small caveat — some lower-level infra ops require separate elevated roles that are not auto-provisioned.
[01:57] Arjun Patel: How granular are the roles? Can we have per-project or per-namespace permissions?
[02:03] Karen Zhou: Yes, RBAC supports per-project access and model-route level controls. There are built-in roles and you can create custom roles with specific capabilities (deploy, read logs, manage keys, etc).
[02:14] Samantha Lee: Audit logs — retention and export. We need to keep logs for seven years for some compliance scenarios. What retention do you provide and how can we export them?
[02:23] Diego Ramos: Default retention in hosted is 90 days for verbose logs, 365 days for aggregated events. For enterprise Dedicated or Private deployments, retention policies can be extended and logs exported to your SIEM (we have native sinks for S3, CloudWatch, and Kafka). For very long-term retention we recommend exporting to your object storage.
[02:44] Noah Kim: Is the export push or pull? We prefer push to our S3 bucket encrypted with our KMS keys.
[02:50] Diego Ramos: Push via S3 sink is supported. We can configure SIEM forwarding and ensure logs are encrypted in transit and at rest. For S3 sink we support using customer-managed KMS keys — so the customer retains key control.
[03:03] Lena Martin: KMS — do you support BYOK? We want to retain control of master keys for any PHI-related data.
[03:09] Karen Zhou: Yes, for Private deployments or Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) using AWS KMS or HSM. For hosted customers we can make arrangements under enterprise contracts for CMK support — typically via cross-account key policies or via bring-your-own key in a partner arrangement.
[03:27] Samantha Lee: Data residency — Can we ensure data is stored only in us-east-1? We have contracts requiring US-only storage.
[03:33] Diego Ramos: We support region pinning for hosted controls for enterprise customers. Also Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) allow you to fully control data residency. For hosted customers we can ensure data-at-rest is stored in specified regions and restrict cross-region replication.
[03:48] Arjun Patel: Controls mapping — we need a spreadsheet mapping Redwood controls to our ISMS controls (SOC 2 criteria + ISO 27001 annex A).
[03:55] Maya Patel: We'll provide a controls mapping template and pre-filled mapping for common controls. Diego will share the full spreadsheet with test procedures and evidence links.
[04:02] Diego Ramos: I'll include where evidence is stored in the Trust Center and sample artifact names so your audit team can find them quickly.
[04:08] Noah Kim: A question on network isolation — if we go Dedicated, can we get private networking and no internet egress?
[04:13] Karen Zhou: Dedicated includes VPC peering options and private endpoints. You can limit egress and require NAT through your network appliances. Private on-prem deployment gives you full network isolation if needed.
[04:23] Samantha Lee: Any SOC 2 exceptions in last 12 months we should be aware of?
[04:27] Diego Ramos: We had a minor control exception related to an internal patching cadence in Q2 last year which is documented in the SOC report and remediated; the remediation steps and timeline are included.
[04:37] Lena Martin: We'll want that noted in our risk register. Also, do you provide attestation for encryption standards used for data at rest?
[04:43] Karen Zhou: Yes, the Trust Center includes crypto standards (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit), key management practices, and where CMKs are used.
[04:50] Arjun Patel: For audit logging retention, can you provide hashes or signatures of exported logs for tamper evidence?
[04:56] Diego Ramos: We don't currently provide signed log bundles by default, but we can work with you to generate signed exports or add log signing as part of a Dedicated/private engagement — it's on our roadmap.
[05:06] Maya Patel: Quick check — timeline and procurement. Crestview, what is your timeline to close and who needs the artifacts?
[05:12] Lena Martin: We're aiming for vendor approval by end of May; need SOC 2, controls mapping, and a short security questionnaire answered by next week for procurement.
[05:21] Samantha Lee: Procurement also needs evidence of SSO/SCIM integration and ability to restrict data residency.
[05:26] Maya Patel: Understood. We'll prioritize the SOC 2 report and the controls mapping. Diego, Karen — anything to add?
[05:33] Karen Zhou: I'll prepare a short runbook for SCIM/SAML configuration and sample Okta mappings.
[05:39] Diego Ramos: I'll attach the controls mapping and a link to the Trust Center with reviewer access; will redact only vendor-internal secrets.
[05:46] Noah Kim: One more on backups — are backups encrypted and where are they stored? We need to know retention and whether backups cross regions.
[05:53] Karen Zhou: Backups are encrypted with customer or Redwood-managed keys depending on deployment; for hosted we can restrict cross-region backups for enterprise contracts. Typically backups are stored in the same region unless you opt into cross-region replication.
[06:07] Arjun Patel: Any questions about penetration testing and vuln disclosures?
[06:11] Diego Ramos: We perform annual pentests and disclose high-severity findings to customers under NDA; the Trust Center contains a summary of recent tests and remediation timelines.
[06:21] Maya Patel: Alright let's capture next steps and action items. We'll send the SOC 2 Type II and Trust Center link via secure share; Diego to attach controls mapping and Karen to send SCIM runbook. Crestview to confirm list of systems needing US-only residency and schedule infra deep dive.
[06:38] Samantha Lee: Sounds good. Also will you provide a signed DPA?
[06:42] Maya Patel: Yes, we have a standard DPA and can provide a signed copy once we have the PO or contract in place.
[06:48] Lena Martin: Thanks, that's helpful.
[06:50] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — we plan to follow up with the artifacts by Thursday. If anything else comes up please reach out.
[06:57] Diego Ramos: End notes: Trust Center link will be: https://trust.redwood.ai/crestview (placeholder), SOC2 report will be shared via secure link.
[07:05] Maya Patel: Meeting close.

Notes on transcription: occasional words may be mis-typed (e.g., SCIM sometimes appears as 'skim' in transcript), proper nouns may be off. Shared artifacts referenced: Trust Center (link above), controls mapping spreadsheet (to be shared), SCIM runbook (to be shared).

End of transcript.
